topics.title: Coursework Conditions & Moodle Statements
topics.summary: Under Assessment Regime Procedure V12 §1.7–1.7.2 and Table 2, Chief Examiners must determine where and how generative AI can be used in a unit or assessment task, clearly publish use specifications in the required LMS section before the teaching period or at least 4 weeks before task details are released (with Table 2 noting a 4-week deadline before the due date / timetable release), and provide educational reasoning when AI is disallowed. Every Moodle assessment task displays one of four standard AI statements.
topics.scope: All Monash coursework assessments across undergraduate and postgraduate units.
actions: Check the Moodle assessment banner before beginning work.
Verify whether the task is classified as 'Without Any Limits', 'Guided', 'Must Not Be Used', or 'Not Applicable'.
If AI is disallowed, the Chief Examiner must provide the educational reasoning in Moodle.

topics.title: Examinations & Supervised Assessments
topics.summary: In all scheduled electronic examinations (eExams), generative AI is strictly prohibited unless explicit permission is granted by the Chief Examiner and displayed on the eExam landing page. Online spell check, grammar, and translation tools are also barred in closed-book and non-open-access exams.
topics.scope: Scheduled final examinations and supervised eExams across all faculties.
actions: Review the eExam instructions on your dashboard prior to commencing the exam session.
Disable all unapproved browser extensions, translation plugins, and generative AI helpers.
Ensure that non-open-access exams are completed without automated grammar or translation tools.

topics.title: Disclosure & Acknowledgment Protocols
topics.summary: When AI use is allowed or required in an assessment, follow its instructions and restrictions, document the type of AI and its contribution, and provide written acknowledgement of use and extent. Cite and reference using the closest appropriate source type when necessary. If AI is permitted but unused, acknowledge non-use. Further tool, version or prompt documentation follows the actual task instructions; no universal prompt-history requirement is established by the cited assessment-use rule.
topics.scope: All student coursework assessments across all faculties.
actions: Include the official Monash AI acknowledgement statement with your submission.
Document all prompts, parameters, and revisions in your working notes.
Submit an explicit non-use confirmation if AI was permitted but you elected not to use it.

Never upload teacher lecture slides, LMS content, or personal sensitive information into AI prompts.

additionalTopics.title: Academic Integrity & Proofreading Boundaries
additionalTopics.summary: Under Student Academic Integrity Procedure, minor, trivial or frivolous breaches due to inappropriate academic practice receive the educative response in §6.1: the Chief Examiner/RO/nominee provides support and a written warning outcome, and awards a mark reflecting the practice without imposing a penalty (§6.1.1). For alleged misconduct, where evidence was not provided with the notice of allegation, students must have a reasonable opportunity of not less than five working days to respond to the allegation and evidence before RO determination (§8.3). Invited students may bring a support person who cannot represent or advocate; at Monash Malaysia a staff member or student may represent them (§8.4). Under §11.1, a finding and penalty, or penalty alone, may be appealed; students who admitted the misconduct may appeal only the penalty. The Hearing and Appeals Panels Procedure governs that process. At Malaysia, §11.2 separately permits a written appeal to the Malaysian Registrar General within 14 days of receiving the decision. Where an academic misconduct allegation occurs WITH a research misconduct allegation, §7.6 instead refers the matter to the research-misconduct RO and this coursework procedure does not investigate or determine it.
